title: Multi-Query Distinguishing of Randomized CBC, CFB, and OFB
summary: A bound is known for one-query attacks, but for multiple queries it remains open whether to find a distinguishing attack or prove a security theorem.

formal_statement.body: In the memory-bounded, block-at-a-time distinguishing model, let $q$ be the number of queries and consider all-zero messages under randomized $\mathrm{CBC}\$$, $\mathrm{CFB}\$$, or $\mathrm{OFB}\$$ instantiated with a random permutation. Each query begins at an independent uniformly random point and reveals successive permutation iterates. A bound is available for one-query attacks; for $q>1$, determine either an attack distinguishing the resulting streams from random streams or a security theorem bounding such distinguishers.

scope.domain: Memory-bounded, block-at-a-time cryptanalysis of randomized symmetric-encryption modes.
assumptions: each query starts at an independent uniformly random point
scope.unresolved_remainder: For q>1, determine either an attack distinguishing the resulting streams from random streams or a security theorem bounding such distinguishers.

citations.label: Tight Time-Memory Trade-Offs for Symmetric Encryption

progress.summary: The source reports a bound for one-query attacks and explicitly states that it does not know an attack or security theorem for the multi-query setting.
citation_labels: Joseph Jaeger et al., Tight Time-Memory Trade-Offs for Symmetric Encryption
